title: Joan Didion's birth chart
metaDescription: Joan Didion's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.0° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the eight placements whose signs are settled, mutable leads with four. Mutable signs end their seasons, and a mutable-heavy chart is read as one built for adaptation and hand-off rather than for standing still.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 13.0° Sagittarius, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mars. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Venus holds 17.1° Sagittarius, Mars holds 27.2° Virgo — in the old shorthand, attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Pluto — a sextile holding at 1.4°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, the Sun square Neptune at 1.5°, and Uranus square Pluto at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Saturn makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks one placement here. Saturn in Aquarius at 22.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: fire 3, earth 2, water 2, air 1 across the elements, and mutable 4, fixed 2, cardinal 2 across the modalities. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. Mercury crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day, so its sign is left open. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.1° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
